title: date_input grey out the year which is within the min_date and max_date range incorrectly
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Year 2016 is greyed out while setting the range between datetime.date(2016, 6, 28) and datetime.date(2018, 4, 13) in date_input.
However, if you first select 1st Jan 2017 and click left arrow at the top left comer, it will show dates in 2016 correctly (un-greyed out) and it can be selected as well. 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b47a71b3-dbb1-4dc5-8644-64523aa8b49f)


### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-9667)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import datetime

test_date = st.sidebar.date_input('Test date', None, datetime.date(2016, 6, 28), datetime.date(2018, 4, 13))
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. go to sidebar
2. click on date_input box
3. click on year drop-down 

### Expected Behavior

year 2016 should be un-greyed and selectable.

### Current Behavior

year 2016 is greyed out and cannot be selected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.38.0
- Python version: 3.12.4
- Operating System: windows
- Browser: edge


### Additional Information

_No response_

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-9667)

Thanks for reporting this issue. I was able to reproduce it [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9667). I think the reason why it is disabled is that you cannot go back to the same month/date of the currently selected month/date. If you select a date that is also allowed in 2016, it seems to work fine. I think this is more of an upstream improvement needed to be implemented in the basweb UI component.

FYI — #14799 was just filed reporting the same issue on Streamlit 1.56.0 (macOS, Safari/Edge), confirming this upstream BaseWeb bug is still present. That issue has a nice side-by-side comparison repro showing the inconsistency clearly.
